en.ru: Люди с синдромом самозванца часто фокусируются на своих неудачах, игнорируя или преуменьшая свои успехи. Это явление связано с когнитивными искажениями, такими как негативный фильтр и дискаунтирование позитивного.
en.oldText: People with impostor syndrome often focus on their failures and minimise or ignore their successes. This is linked to cognitive distortions such as a negative mental filter and “discounting the positives”.
en.newText: People with imposter syndrome often focus on their failures while ignoring or downplaying their successes. This phenomenon is linked to cognitive distortions, such as a mental filter and discounting the positive.

passes.reason: Translation B is more idiomatic and follows the project's terminology guidelines perfectly. Translation A uses 'discounting the positives' (plural) and unnecessary quotation marks, whereas B uses the canonical singular form 'discounting the positive' as required.

issues.note: Uses 'discounting the positives' instead of the standard 'discounting the positive'.
The use of quotation marks around the term is unnecessary and looks less professional in a psychological context.

passes.reason: Translation A follows the glossary perfectly (mental filter, discounting the positive) and flows naturally. Translation B uses 'minimise' which is less idiomatic here than 'downplaying', and adds unnecessary quotation marks and a plural 'positives' which deviates from the standard CBT term.

en.ru: Исследования показывают, что позитивное подкрепление и поддержка со стороны окружающих могут значительно уменьшить уровень тревоги и повысить уверенность в своих силах. Развитие навыков самоподдержки и осознанности также помогает справляться с синдромом самозванца.
en.oldText: Research shows that supportive feedback and encouragement from others can significantly reduce anxiety and boost confidence. Developing skills of self-support and mindfulness also helps in coping with impostor feelings.
en.newText: Research shows that positive reinforcement and support from others can significantly reduce anxiety levels and increase confidence. Developing self-support and mindfulness skills also helps in managing imposter syndrome.

passes.reason: Translation B uses the correct psychological term 'imposter syndrome' and follows the natural flow of English scientific/educational prose. Translation A uses 'impostor feelings', which is a weaker, less professional phrasing.

issues.note: Used 'impostor feelings' instead of the standard 'imposter syndrome'.
The phrase 'Developing skills of self-support' is slightly clunky compared to the more natural 'Developing self-support skills'.
